newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese urged to donate blood free of charge.
newsitem.headline: Chinese urged to donate blood free of charge.

text.p: Chinese health authorities are urging people to start giving blood free of charge to try to guarantee blood quality and make up for a shortage in hospitals, officials and state media said on Wednesday.

The Red Cross Society of China has launched a drive to encourage more people to donate blood for humanitarian reasons rather than for money, vice-chairwoman of the Red Cross Society of China, Sun Baiqiu, told Reuters.
"Only the blood from unpaid donations is the most safe and any donation for profit will involve unsafe factors," Sun said.
Now, most Chinese blood donors could obtain 1,000-2,000 yuan ($120-240) as well as a long holiday from their work units for a single donation, she said.
Some donors just wanted money and did not care whether they had such problems as anaemia or hepatitis or even if they were infected by HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, Sun said.

China has begun a drive to test all blood products since the discovery in April of some samples of an HIV-contaminated product manufactured and sold in the southern province of Guangdong, media reports said last week.
The Red Cross official said this incident was an example of a case that resulted from commercial blood donations, but declined to give further details.
The official said China's blood supply lagged far behind domestic needs because of the huge population of 1.2 billion, adding that free donations could help relieve the gap between supply and demand.
"Free blood donation should be the way out for China's blood programme," the China Daily quoted Sun Baiqiu as saying.
